units.en: Most easily done with historical focuses turned off; Japan can potentially go Hokushin-ron, which leads to them making a non-aggression pact with you and attacking the USSR instead. Can be combined with "It's all coming together" and "A Fullmetal Brotherhood" if played safely. Keep in mind that it's just China's starting coastal states & not all their cores, so you can afford to lose coastal states that you conquer later (be careful with Qingdao though, it's a one province state so it can easily be lost by mistake).

As with all capitulation achievements, you need to be careful; Even if you've occupied most of a country's territory, they can capitulate to another country if that country has a greater war contribution score. The Germans will not begin Operation Barbarossa so long as France hasn't capitulated, so France's survival is your best bet to ensure Soviet neutrality. Germany's main strength lies in their air force, so build plenty of high-quality fighters and equip divisions with anti-air guns. You can't get this achievement if Germany isn't fascist anymore, so don't try it on ahistorical.

Czecho-Slovak Republic

The cosmetic tag can only be gained via the "The Fall of the Republic" event chain while being democratic. The event chain starts once Germany gains the Sudetenland via their Demand Sudetenland focus, after Czechoslovakia has been betrayed by their allies. 6 days after the initial event the second event will trigger and immediately change your name. If you select the "We need radical change" option in that event your name will also change to "Czecho-Slovak Republic", which is redundant due to the immediate effect of the event. Furthermore, 14 days after the second event a third event will demand you release Slovakia as a puppet. Releasing Slovakia will again also change your name (which is also redundant). You don't actually have to release Slovakia to gain this achievement, but it could prove useful to use them as a buffer state by not calling them into the war. For detailed strategies, see I didn't hear no bell

Et tu, Paulus?Capture a field Marshal.
Has captured an enemy field marshal

On historical, Finland deploys their general Aksel Airo in mid '37. The Finnish AI is highly inclined to promote him to field marshal, but once they do this they will un-deploy him as an HQ and deploy someone else. However, if you justify on them as the Soviets at game start and just encircle him immediately, the HQ will be unable to disband. From here, you just have to keep him encircled & make sure the HQ doesn't kill itself before ~1938 - at around this time, Finland should promote Airo despite being encircled, and then you can capture him. There's no way to tell whether he has been promoted or not, but waiting until around mid 1938 will make it more consistent. On historical, Switzerland also at one point deploys their field marshal and will leave him in the field at least till 1945.
